title: Google AI data center project investigated after 420 football fields of Finnish forest razed — trees were removed before a mandatory environmental impact assessment, say reports
source_used: AFP's text as carried by Daily Sabah (4 Oct 2026), and Tom's Hardware (pool link, fetched text), which relays AFP
key_facts: AFP reported from Muhos, a northern Finnish town of about 8,800 people, that the Finnish Supervisory Agency (LVV) is investigating whether Tuike Finland, which represents Google, cleared more than 300 hectares of forest without a mandatory environmental impact assessment.

Hanna Halmeenpaa, chair of the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation, who filed the request with the agency, said work at the site should be suspended until it is clarified whether the project follows the law.
She said satellite images show nature sites that should be preserved were also logged, and that the clear-cut area is comparable to 420 football fields.

Google told AFP the tree felling complied with Forestry Act requirements and that it was awaiting further guidance from the agency; its Finland communications manager said high-value nature zones were protected.
The site is part of Google's announced 13 billion euro ($15 billion) investment in Finland over two years, its biggest in Europe, which also covers Kajaani, Vaala and Hamina.
A citizens' initiative demanding stricter rules on data centre energy use and environmental effects gathered more than 50,000 signatures in three days, so parliament must review it.
Tom's Hardware relayed the AFP report on 5 Oct 2026 with commentary and no new facts; AFP's own report ran on 4 Oct 2026.
quote_evidence: The Finnish Supervisory Agency (LVV) is currently investigating whether the company Tuike Finland, which represents Google, had cleared more than 300 hectares of forest in Muhos without a mandatory environmental impact assessment.

Google, meanwhile, told AFP in an email that "tree felling activities have been taking place in compliance with Forestry Act requirements" and they "were awaiting further guidance from LVV on this matter."
Google’s latest data center construction project in Finland is being investigated after the company representing the search giant allegedly cleared over 300 hectares of forest.
why_it_matters_hint: A test of whether forest can be cleared for a data center before its environmental review, with the agency yet to rule and Google saying the felling was lawful.
event_date: AFP report of 4 Oct 2026; Tom's Hardware relay of 5 Oct 2026. The date the felling happened is not stated.
notes: Follow-up of our 4 Oct 2026 pool item C09-11 (AFP, 'Finnish town braces for change from Google data centres', score 4, pool only), which is the same AFP report; it was not printed in any earlier edition. Tom's Hardware adds commentary and no new fact. AFP is the first reporter; the AFP text was read as carried by Daily Sabah, so the url points there.
